To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the immune function of the convalescent SARC patients was normal, but some patients had an abnormal counting and lymphocyte activity of the lymphocyte subgroup, which should be followed for a long period.

the immune function of the SARS convalescent patients was normal, but some patients showed abnormal distribution of lymphocyte groups and lymphocyte activity, and the content of Ag NOR correlated with the number of CD3+, NK, CD3+HLA DR+, and CD3+CD25+.

the number of the total and CD4 + T lymphocytes was almost normal, the number of CD8 + T lymphocytes increased, the ratio of CD4+/CD8+ decreased, and the number of B lymphocyte was normal, the number NK cell decreased in the patients with SARS, and the number and activity of T lymphocyte were abnormal in the patients with severe SARS, especially in those older than age 50 years or treated with high dose hormones.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the immune function of the peripheral blood lymphocytes in the patients with SARS.
the distribution of lymphocytes subgroups and its relationship to the content of Ag NOR in patients with convalescence of SARS.
the immune status of the patients with SARS convalescence and their immune function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lymphocyte subpopulation and its active state of the patients with SARS were in normal range and the immune system of the body was normal.
the lymphocyte subpopulation and the Ag NOR content of the patients with SARS were normal, but there was a tendency to decrease in some of them.
the immune state of patients with convalecent SARS is normal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lymphocyte subpopu-lation in patients with convalescence SARS is in a state of active immune response.
the lymphocyte subpopulatons in patients with convalescence SARS were in a state of relative immune depression.
the immune state of patients with convalesce SARS is normal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immune function of the patient with convalescent of SARS was not normal.
the lymphocyte subpopulatons and the lymphocyte activity in the patients with SARS are normal.
the immune function of convalescent patients with SARS is normal.
